The paper introduces SR-AR and SR-CQLR procedures for linear and nonlinear moment-condition models and establishes their asymptotic size and similarity properties.

The paper formulates weak identification through weakly regular parameters and establishes the role of an underlying regular parameter.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace the square-root covariance factor chart with a collision-regular observable chart, or prove an explicit DDD implementation whose estimator of (K,a) remains uniformly asymptotically linear as Omega loses rank; then restate the envelope theorem over that nonempty application class.

Give a finite algorithm for the exact-null search, envelope supremum, and atom rule, with a complexity or termination statement and a derived simulation-error bound instead of placing solver accuracy wholly in admissibility.

Work out one small retained-score DDD instance with a genuine rank-loss path, verify every admissibility condition there, and numerically or analytically compare its envelope power with the fixed-rank plug-in and SR-style calibration.
